description: Browse food and beverage video templates and rebuild any of them around the product you sell. No prompt to write. Download a file you can post in minutes.
h1: Food and Beverage Video Templates You Can Recreate
lead: Browse food and beverage video templates and rebuild any of them around your product, in minutes, with no prompt to write.
steps_h2: How to Make a Food and Drink Video in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Add the package you sell, name the moment, and download a file you can post.

steps.d: Add the package photo already on your listing. The template wraps the ad around that product.
Name the moment in a short line, such as the pour or the first sip. The shot is already set.
Download a tall file for a phone, or a square for the product page, and post it.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of starting from a blank file?
faq.a: A template already sets the scene and ad structure. Add your drink and message to make the video sooner.

faq.q: Can I use the pour in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Use the watermark-free video in paid ads, social posts, product pages, or client work. Commercial use is included.

faq.q: How much does a drink template ad cost?
faq.a: A 6-second video costs 24 credits, 10 seconds costs 40, 15 costs 60, and 30 costs 120. Starter costs $24.50 for 200 credits.

faq.q: Which placements fit a pour ad?
faq.a: Post a tall version on TikTok or Reels, a square version on feeds, or a wide version on YouTube. Choose the size for each placement.

faq.q: Who is a drink template for?
faq.a: It is for drink brands, shops, and marketers who need ads quickly. Start with one product or make versions for a larger campaign.
Cans, bottles, cartons, and other packaged drinks work. Choose a scene that shows the product clearly and matches your offer.

faq.q: How does a drink template become a video?
faq.a: Upload your package image, choose the template, and change the message. The tool makes a finished video with a voice and visuals.

faq.q: What is a food and drink ad template?
faq.a: It is a ready-made video format for showing a drink or packaged food. Add your product to make a creator-style ad in minutes without filming.

faq.q: Can I use my own package photo and logo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your own package photo, logo, or video. The template keeps your product at the center of the ad.

faq.q: Can a first-timer make a pour ad?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear package photo and follow a few steps. You do not need filming or editing experience.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of filming a creator?
faq.a: Templates let you make drink ads in minutes without hiring a creator. Try different openings and offers without waiting for another shoot.

steps.prompt: A hand pours citrus soda from the silver can into one glass filled with ice. The shot starts at counter height and moves closer as the glass fills. Bright window light stays beside the can. The can and the full glass are both in the last shot. You hear a crisp fizz and a soft pour. Add background music if you want it. Keep the can's shape, color, and label as in your photo.

definition.title: What Is a Food and Drink Ad Template?
paras: A food and drink template is a ready ad for one moment, built around the package you sell. You add the product. You do not build the shot from nothing.
An AI actor can hold the glass, and a spoken voice can read the line you write. You can ask for a draft line if you would rather not write it.

reasons.h2: Why Sellers Start From a Template
reasons.lead: A new flavor can go out in an ad without a kitchen booking or a creator on the calendar.

items.d: The scene runs from the package photo you already have, so the ad does not wait on a kitchen or a person on camera.

items.t: Credits Instead of a Shoot Fee
items.d: New cuts spend credits on the plan that fits your volume. Money you skip on a crew can go toward reaching buyers.

items.t: More Than One Cut to Test
items.d: Make a second opening and a second language from the same package photo. Keep the cut you want to run.

items.t: Change the Line and Render Again
items.d: Change the flavor name or the offer and render again. Fixing a word does not mean calling a creator back.

items.t: No Hold on a Creator Calendar
items.d: The pour scene is ready when the flavor is ready, including one you added late in the week.
You spend the words on the flavor. The glass, the timing, and where the package sits are already in the template.

more_sections.lead: A spoken voice, words on screen, music, and publishing sit with the template, so you finish in one place.

items.t: A Spoken Voice on the Pour
items.d: A ready voice can name the flavor out loud, in the language you sell in.

items.t: Words You Can Move on Screen
items.d: The flavor line can sit on screen, and you can slide it in the editor before you export.
The same scene can serve each product you sell, so one look becomes more than one ad.
